Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the days to resolve a complaint, to reply to a review and to start a renewal, the credit the owner must approve and the jobs of the last 90 days.

Check Clients, Team, Crews and Complaint Kinds: every client has a type, a frequency, a start and a lead source. A labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour and a crew is the cleaners who work together on a job.

Write every complaint on Complaints: the job, the client, the kind, the priority and the credit. The days open, the resolved-in-time check and the response check fill in by themselves; Complaint Triage works out the priority first.
A re-clean is a free return visit to fix a problem: write each one on Re-cleans with the hours and the cost, and give a credit on Service Credits when the client needs one.

Write every review on Reviews and the reply on Review Replies; the stars, the days to reply and the low rating flag fill in by themselves. Satisfaction Surveys keep the scores from 1 to 5 for quality, punctuality, communication and value.
Keep every yearly office contract on Contracts. The days to the end, the yearly value and the renewal check show which contracts need a renewal and which ended without one.
Follow each renewal on Renewal Steps, change the price on Contract Price Reviews and log each week on Contract Visit Log so missed visits never go unseen. Office Client Notes keep the follow-ups.
When a client leaves write them on Lost Clients with the reason, then use Win-back Offers. Referrals and Client Milestones show who brings you new clients and how long they stay.

Use the 14 calculators when you plan: triage, credit, re-clean cost, review reply, recommend score, lifetime value, churn cost, renewal price, contract value, renewal timing, referral reward, retention, win-back and a what-if grid.
Read the Retention Dashboard and Charts every week. Contract, credit and complaint rules differ by place: check your own local rules before you use any sample wording.

Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the wanted margin, the utilization target, the cash floor, the owner draw and the share of profit you set aside for tax.

Read Client Profit first. A labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour and a crew is the cleaners who work together on a job. Each client shows profit, margin and the price a visit needs for your target margin.
Check Service Months, Profit by Area, Profit by Client Type and Jobs to see which service, area, client type and job earns and which loses money.
Enter every overhead payment on Expenses and set a monthly budget for each category on Budget; the actual amount, the difference and the flag fill in by themselves.
Fill in Monthly Summary each month: the invoiced amount, the cash received, crew pay, supplies, expenses and the tax you set aside; the operating profit and margin are calculated.
Follow the money on Cash and Owner Draw Plan: the closing cash, the net cash flow, the cash left after the draw and a check against your cash floor.
Keep Taxes up to date with the period, the base, the rate and the due date (business tax instalments and payroll tax: check your own local rules); the days to the due date fill in by themselves.
Use Marketing, Lead Sources and Quotes Won by Month to see the cost per lead and per new client, and Growth Targets, Forecast, Break-even and Leases and Loans to plan the next months.
